To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

variation in women's judgments about the personality characteristics of masculine men predicts variation in the effect of the relationship context on women’s preferences for men with masculine pitch in their voices.

the extent to the extent to which a masculine male voice is perceived to be physically dominant and low in trustworthiness predicts the extent to which the voice is perceived to have a more desirable pitch as a potential short-term partner than as a potential long-term partner, and this relationship between voice pitch and relationship context is stronger among women who report stronger preferences for masculine voices as short-term partners.

variation in women's perceptions of the personality characteristics of masculine men predicts individual variation in the magnitude of women's preferences for low (i.e. masculine) pitch as a function of relationship context.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how individual differences in women’s perceptions of the personality of men with masculine voices influence the effect of relationship type on their masculinity preferences.
the role that perceived personality attributions may play in the development of individual differences in women’s mate preferences.
how individual differences in women shape their mate preferences and the implications of these individual differences for women's mating decisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Variation in perceptions of physical masculinity predicts individual differences in women s preferences for men with masculine voices as short term partners than as long term partners, highlighting the importance for perceived personality attributions in women s judgments of men s vocal attractiveness.

the variation in the extent that women prefer low pitch men as short-term partner than as long-term partner is associated with their perceptions of the physical dominance and trust worthiness of men with low pitch voices.

the extent to what women attribute low trustworthiness and physical dominance to masculine voices predicts their individual differences in the preference for masculine pitch in short-term relationships.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
variation in women's personality judgments of men predicts variation in their vocal attractiveness judgments.

variation in the effect of context on women's mate preferences may be driven by individual differences in the degree to which women perceive masculinity to signal negative personality characteristics that are less costly for women in short-term relationships.
women's preferences for men's voices are influenced by their own individual differences in personality and that this influence is mediated by the perceived personality traits of the voice.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the extent to a woman perceives men as physically dominant and untrustworthy is associated with the magnitude of her preference for masculine pitch in a man's voice as a short-term versus a long-term mate.
women who attribute antisocial traits to men with masculine voices may have a stronger preference for masculine men as a short-term partner than as a long-term partner.
women's perceptions of men's personality characteristics are a key factor in explaining individual differences in women’s preferences for men with masculine voices.
